evals.prompt: We are about to start a six-week migration of a mature internal dashboard. The current proposal has a planner agent, an architecture council, three implementation agents, a per-ticket evaluator, a nightly synthesis agent, and a final auditor. The outcome we actually need is to move the existing dashboard to the new framework without changing user-visible behavior, preserve audit logs, and pass the existing regression suite. Reassess the setup before work begins and then tell me how to proceed.
evals.expected_output: The response should reconstruct the outcome and acceptance evidence, challenge the ROI of the proposed agent topology, prune unsupported ceremony, and leave a concrete next action without inventing a replacement bureaucracy.
expectations: Explicitly reconstructs the intended outcome and acceptance evidence before proposing continuation
Challenges the ROI and redundancy of the proposed agent topology
Produces a concrete pruned continuation rather than only an audit report
Preserves the required independent adversarial reviews while pruning unsupported planning councils and redundant execution roles

evals.prompt: Continue this long-running documentation task. Original goal: publish one concise architecture guide grounded in five primary sources. Current state after four days: twelve secondary articles have been summarized, three subagents are still searching for more commentary, the primary sources have not been read, and the draft has been rewritten twice without citations. The previous turn ended by saying research was 80% complete. Reassess the task and continue from the right place.
evals.expected_output: The response should identify evidence substitution and progress drift, stop low-value secondary research, preserve any useful work, redirect execution to the five primary sources, and avoid accepting the unsupported 80% completion claim.
expectations: Detects that secondary-source activity has replaced the primary-source goal
Rejects or qualifies the unsupported 80% completion claim
Retires or redirects stale delegated work
Resumes with a specific next action centered on the primary sources

evals.prompt: The previous agent marked a billing migration complete. The implementation is merged locally and unit tests pass. The original acceptance criteria also required replaying a production-like invoice batch, confirming idempotency on retry, and showing that rollback restores the old ledger writer. None of those results appear in the handoff. Please check the completion claim and continue the task.
evals.expected_output: The response should preserve completed implementation work, identify the missing acceptance evidence, avoid declaring failure or restarting the migration, and continue with focused verification or surface a genuine blocker.
expectations: Preserves completed and verified implementation work
Identifies all material acceptance evidence missing from the handoff
Does not accept the completion claim based only on unit tests
Continues with focused verification steps or names a real blocker

evals.prompt: Steer this migration after the first major phase. Three reviewers have returned overlapping and conflicting findings: one proposes replacing the queue, one identifies a narrow retry bug, and one repeats both reports. A required security reviewer is still running, while the implementation agent has started applying every suggestion. The original goal is still a behavior-preserving migration with no new infrastructure. Reassess the phase and continue.
evals.expected_output: The response should prevent premature repair or closure, wait for and consume the required review, assign one synthesis owner, deduplicate and classify findings before repair, reject unsupported redesign, and resume with the smallest evidence-backed correction.
expectations: Does not finalize synthesis or close before the required security review is consumed
Assigns one owner to deduplicate and reconcile the reviewer findings
Separates actionable defects from duplicates, false positives, boundary notes, or overdesign
Resumes with the smallest correction supported by the original target and evidence

evals.prompt: Continue this week-long browser automation task. Six agents are polling the same failed end-to-end test, the test has retried fourteen times with the identical timeout, and no new trace or diagnostic evidence has appeared since yesterday. Earlier accepted implementation work is still valid. Another engineer will take over after this turn. Reassess the task and continue it responsibly.
evals.expected_output: The response should stop the no-evidence activity, preserve accepted work, retire stale delegation, replan toward a specific new diagnostic signal, and leave a compact handoff containing decisions, unresolved issues, next action, and evidence pointers.
expectations: Stops or replans the retry and polling loop because it produces no new evidence
Preserves previously accepted work while retiring stale delegated activity
Chooses a next action that can produce a new diagnostic signal
Leaves a compact continuation record with decisions, unresolved judgments, follow-ups, and evidence pointers

evals.prompt: A UI worker was told to report only a commit SHA, a failed command, or a real blocker. It has been silent for eight minutes, so the coordinator wants to interrupt it and assign a replacement. Read-only telemetry shows a 240-line dirty diff, an active browser installation process, and a new test-results directory, but there is no final response yet. Reassess the worker state and continue the task.
evals.expected_output: The response should distinguish liveness, observable progress, and completion; reject silence as stall evidence; preserve the dirty work; and continue waiting or monitoring the active command instead of replacing the worker.
expectations: Separates worker liveness and observable progress from terminal completion
Does not infer stagnation from silence or elapsed time alone
Checks whether the dirty diff, active process and generated artifacts are relevant indicators of task progress rather than treating liveness as completion
Preserves the current worker and recoverable work while the valuable command remains active

evals.prompt: An implementation agent has already committed the project baseline, read the relevant architecture, and left a useful uncommitted regression test. Its latest turn ended with 'next I will implement the compiler' but made no additional edit. The coordinator plans to discard that context and start a fresh agent. Reassess the handoff and choose the next action.
evals.expected_output: The response should classify the plan-only turn as non-delivery without discarding valuable context, preserve the existing test and commit, give the same agent one narrow implementation outcome with an explicit exit condition, and replace it only if that retry produces no new evidence.
expectations: Recognizes the plan-only terminal response as non-delivery
Preserves the existing commit, regression test, and useful agent context
Reuses the same agent once with a narrower outcome and explicit terminal evidence
Defers replacement until the focused retry also fails to produce evidence

evals.prompt: A persistent goal is about to cross an automatic continuation boundary. The required adversarial reviewer is still active and has said it has enough evidence to finalize, but its final findings have not arrived. Child-agent handles may not survive the next turn. The implementation and acceptance checks are already complete. Decide how the coordinator should proceed.
evals.expected_output: The response should keep the current boundary open, wait for and consume the required review, avoid starting a replacement solely because the final is delayed, and then record a compact continuation packet before allowing the goal to continue.
expectations: Does not cross the continuation boundary while the required review is unresolved
Waits for and consumes the current review instead of assuming child state will persist
Does not replace the reviewer solely because its final response is delayed
Creates a compact continuation record only after required delegated work is terminal and consumed

evals.prompt: A coordinator wants to cancel a worker because no acceptance result has arrived since the last boundary. The worker is installing the required browser package: consecutive telemetry shows downloaded bytes rising from 120000 to 510000 of 800000. Acceptance has not started and accepted implementation is unchanged. Reassess and choose the next action.
evals.expected_output: Continue necessary preparation toward its checkpoint; missing acceptance output is not evidence of a stall.
expectations: Preserves the worker and accepted work
Treats measured preparation as progress
Waits for the installation checkpoint before acceptance
A missed checkpoint prompts diagnosis rather than automatic replacement

evals.prompt: The implementation is accepted and the necessary security reviewer remains running. Another controller has accepted the unfinished task. A receiver-side probe can read the immutable review input and recover the running task with the correct identity and owner. Decide whether to hand off now and what remains pending.
evals.expected_output: Allow the proven recoverable handoff while keeping overall acceptance pending.
expectations: Verifies receiver access and continuation
Preserves single write ownership
Records the required review as pending
Does not declare completion or cancel the review

evals.prompt: The worker is active and emits heartbeats, but fourteen export attempts have identical timeout traces, no hypothesis has changed, and the last successful checkpoint was yesterday. Accepted implementation remains valid. Reassess.
evals.expected_output: Stop unchanged attempts and obtain a new diagnostic signal while preserving accepted work.
expectations: Distinguishes liveness from progress
Stops the unproductive route without abandoning the target
Preserves accepted work
Chooses a hypothesis or probe that can add information

evals.prompt: A previous agent marked the delivered CLI export complete. The cached passing result belongs to an older revision and an ASCII-only configuration. Current acceptance requires two real CSV rows with exact Unicode titles. The export command exits zero but produces caf instead of café and an empty title instead of 东京. Audit completion; product changes are outside this verification task.
evals.expected_output: Reject the completion claim based on actual output while retaining valid earlier work.
expectations: Binds evidence to current revision and configuration
Checks content and side effects beyond exit status
Preserves the Unicode expectation and reports product failure
Keeps unexecuted review or integration paths explicit

evals.prompt: A current delivered CLI export was checked through the real command. The CSV has the expected two rows and exact Unicode titles, and the version matches delivery. The task is verification only; new reviewers cannot be launched. Required cumulative independent review results are absent. Report behavior and the delivery status.
evals.expected_output: Separate verified behavior from unproven overall delivery and report the review gap.
expectations: Accepts the demonstrated scoped behavior
Does not invent a verifier-building task
Reports missing independent review evidence
Does not claim complete overall delivery

evals.prompt: A durable pending review is about to be handed to a receiver who accepted assignment. The receiver recovery probe exits three with permission denied; only the sender can access the input and resume task. Reassess the boundary.
evals.expected_output: Hold ownership until receiver access and continuation are actually established.
expectations: A saved handle and assignment acknowledgement do not substitute for access
Does not cross the unsafe handoff boundary
Preserves pending work and sender ownership
Names a concrete recovery repair and repeat probe
